title: Unicode-Aware Palindrome
hints: Lowercase the text, keep only letters and numbers, then compare it with its reverse.
jsBridge: JS would lowercase and strip with a regex like `/[^a-z0-9]/gi`, which is ASCII-only. Swift's `Character.isLetter` and `isNumber` are Unicode-aware, so accented letters and other scripts work, and `lowercased()` handles more than ASCII.

compass.q: Your JS regex `[a-z0-9]` breaks for "Ésope reste ici et se repose". What does Swift's `isLetter` do differently?
Is `Array(s) == Array(s).reversed()` correct for strings with combining accents? What if one side uses a precomposed é and the other e + ◌́?
